issues.legal_issue: A distinct coke oven plant used to manufacture hard coke does not vest with a nationalised coal mine merely because it is located in or associated with the mine.
material_facts: The coal mine and coke oven had been transferred and leased separately.
The mine was nationalised, but no action was taken to nationalise the coke oven plant.
The coke oven was a significant facility for manufacturing hard coke, not merely minor equipment subsidiary to the mining operation.
issues.conclusion: The coke oven plant was distinct from the mine and did not vest in the Central Government by virtue of the mine’s nationalisation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3(b) and 3(j), including clauses 3(j)(vi) and 3(j)(x), establish a statutory distinction between a coke oven plant and a mine. A facility for manufacturing hard coke with an independent existence is not treated as part of a mine merely because it is associated with mining; minor equipment used for washing coal or manufacturing coke may fall within the definition of a mine. The court rejected the argument based on section 8 of the Transfer of Property Act. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.appeal_from_lower_court_judgment: A party appealed from a lower court’s judgment concerning the treatment of a coke oven associated with a coal mine.
predicates.coal_mine_nationalised: The coal mine was taken over through nationalisation.
predicates.coke_oven_plant_not_separately_nationali: No separate step was taken to nationalise the coke oven plant.
predicates.hard_coke_facility_has_independent_exist: The facility was a significant, independently existing operation for manufacturing hard coke rather than minor equipment subsidiary to mining.

issues.definition: When a lower-court appeal concerns a nationalised mine, no separate nationalisation of the coke oven plant occurred, and the hard-coke facility has an independent existence, the separate plant does not vest with the mine.

issues.legal_issue: Ownership of a coke oven remains with its owner where the transfer documents reserve ownership and grant the transferee only a lease of the coke oven.
material_facts: The owner transferred the coal mine to a company and granted the same company a lease of the coke oven.
The documents showed that ownership of the coke oven was retained by the owner.
issues.conclusion: The owner retained ownership of the coke oven; it had not been transferred along with the coal mine.
issues.legal_principle: The court determined ownership from the transfer and lease documents and found that they disclosed retention of the coke oven by its owner. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: appeal_from_lower_court_judgment and mine_transferred_to_transferee and coke_oven_leased_to_transferee and documents_reserve_coke_oven_ownership

predicates.appeal_from_lower_court_judgment: A party appealed from a lower court’s judgment concerning ownership of a coke oven associated with a transferred mine.
predicates.mine_transferred_to_transferee: The owner transferred the coal mine to another person or entity.
predicates.coke_oven_leased_to_transferee: The owner granted the recipient of the mine a lease of the coke oven.
predicates.documents_reserve_coke_oven_ownership: The transfer and lease documents show that ownership of the coke oven was retained by the transferor.

issues.definition: When a mine is transferred, its coke oven is leased to the transferee, and the documents reserve ownership of the oven, the transferor retains ownership.

issues.legal_issue: The Central Government must pay rent for its use of a coke oven plant that remained owned by another person, at a reduced rate fixed by the court in resolving the dispute.
material_facts: The coal mine vested in the Central Government upon nationalisation, but the coke oven plant remained owned by the plaintiff.
The plaintiff had leased the coke oven, and the Central Government resisted liability for rent.
The parties left the court to determine a fair rent, and the respondents agreed to a reduction from the rent stipulated in the lease.
The court considered the possible difficulty arising from section 9 of the Act and fixed rent at one-third of the stipulated rent.
issues.conclusion: The Central Government was liable to pay rent for the coke oven at one-third of the rent stipulated in the lease.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered section 9 of the Coking Coal Mines (Nationalisation) Act, 1972, as potentially affecting liability for obligations arising from an encumbrance. In the circumstances, and following the parties’ agreement to reduce the rent, it fixed a fair rent at one-third of the stipulated amount. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: appeal_from_lower_court_judgment and coke_oven_remains_owned_by_lessor and government_uses_leased_coke_oven_after_mine_nationalisation and parties_leave_fair_rent_to_court

predicates.appeal_from_lower_court_judgment: A party appealed from a lower court’s judgment concerning rent for a leased coke oven after nationalisation of an associated mine.
predicates.coke_oven_remains_owned_by_lessor: The person who leased the coke oven continued to own it.
predicates.government_uses_leased_coke_oven_after_m: After the associated mine was nationalised, the government used the leased coke oven.
predicates.parties_leave_fair_rent_to_court: The parties left it to the court to determine a fair rent and agreed to a reduction from the stipulated rent.

issues.definition: When the lessor retains ownership, the government uses the leased coke oven after mine nationalisation, and the parties leave fair rent to the court, the government must pay reduced lease rent.
